starbridge ask \
  --question 'How long should acme notes sync keep deleted notes in trash before auto-purge: 7, 30, or 90 days?' \
  --context 'Deleted notes never leave the trash and the storage bill doubled.
7 days: cheapest, but misses restores after a week. 85% of restore requests come within 3 weeks.
30 days: covers most restore requests (85% arrive within 3 weeks). Recommended.
90 days: longest restore window, highest storage cost. Each month of trash costs about $20 at current volume.' \
  --option '7 days' --option '30 days' --option '90 days' \
  --waiting 2>&1; echo "exit=$?"
turns.final:
Trash now auto-purges notes older than 7 days. The owner picked 7 days through a Starbridge card.

Changes in `src/trash.js`:
- `purgeExpired(retentionMs, now)` drops entries older than the window.
- `TRASH_RETENTION_MS` is set to 7 days.
- `remove()` runs the purge before adding each new deletion.

I checked the purge with sample entries: an entry 10 days old was dropped, and one 3 days old was kept. Nothing else in the repo was tested because there is no test setup.

Two things to know:
- **Purge only runs on deletes.** The repo has no scheduler or entry point, so if no one deletes a note, expired entries stay until the next delete. If you have a scheduler elsewhere, call `purgeExpired(TRASH_RETENTION_MS)` there too.
- **The card had no recommendation marked.** I left out `--recommended`, so the card showed no suggested option. I didn't repost it to fix that.
